standard.title: Improvise and devise drama
standard.description: improvise and/or devise and shape drama using the elements of drama to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can create and co-create fictional situations using elements of drama in dramatic play and process drama (Y1-2). They can take on roles, contribute ideas, and communicate non-verbally within a group improvisation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students improvise and/or devise and shape drama using elements of drama to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning.

nodes.label: Identifying dramatic potential
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a situation, issue or story worth exploring through drama and name what ideas or perspectives it raises.
nodes.minimum_width: Student identifies one scenario or situation from a given starting point (story, image, issue) and names what they want to explore through drama.
nodes.typical_width: Students create drama by exploring and experiencing roles and situations they initiate and develop; they consider how empathy assists them to take on roles and 'stand in the shoes' of another; they explore roles in a 'miniature world' or from everyday interactions.
wider: Students improvise drama exploring situations from another time or place, imagining themselves as participants in an event
Students devise dialogue for a previously 'wordless story' or dramatic action for a story known only through spoken/audio sources
Students devise drama communicating their connection to a place in their community, drawing on First Nations Australians' drama about Country/Place as a starting point
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot identify what a drama might be about — cannot articulate the idea, perspective or meaning they want to explore — shaping and devising collapses into random action; the purpose-driven crafting in subsequent nodes depends on this.

response_modes.reason: Use guiding questions ('What is this story really about?', 'What do you want an audience to think or feel?', 'Whose perspective are you exploring?') before improvisation begins.
Offer varied stimulus material — images, texts, community contexts, historical moments — to ensure students with different entry points can each find genuine dramatic potential.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of perspectives, issues and human situations available as dramatic starting points is very broad; students who explore widely develop stronger ability to find and communicate ideas through drama.
success_criteria: Student names a situation or perspective they want to explore through their drama
Student can explain what ideas or feelings their drama is trying to communicate

nodes.label: Using elements to shape improvised drama
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use elements of drama — time, place, role, language, movement — to shape improvisations and give them meaning and structure.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least one deliberate choice about how to use an element (e.g. changing place, pace, or character relationship) to shape the drama.
nodes.typical_width: Students use elements of drama and principles of story (establishing time, place, roles and characters) to shape improvisations; they experiment with voice (loudness, pace, pitch) and movement to create roles and situations; they explore heightening tension through language and spatial awareness.
wider: Students experiment with ways to connect short scenes (rhythmic patterns, transition phrases, movement sequences)
Students explore how developing spatial awareness — distance, proximity, stillness — can manipulate tension in dramatic action

response_modes.reason: Students need a growing repertoire of element-based choices to draw on; provide frequent short improvisation tasks that each focus on one element, building command of the full kit.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one deliberate element-based choice when shaping improvised drama
Student can name the element they used and what effect it had on the drama

nodes.label: Devising and presenting drama with communicative intent
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can work collaboratively to devise a structured drama that communicates an intended idea, perspective or meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Student contributes to devising a drama (with at least one other student) that has a clear beginning, development and ending, and communicates a recognisable idea.
nodes.typical_width: Students work in groups to devise sections of drama and then, working as a class, combine sections using a play-building process; they communicate their connection to Country/Place through Acknowledgement of Country (as appropriate); they shape improvisation to communicate their intentions as drama-makers.
wider: Students devise drama exploring issues and ideas, using empathy to consider multiple perspectives and challenge their own assumptions
Students devise drama based on a real or imagined 'miniature world', developing a complex fictional space with consistent roles, rules and relationships

response_modes.reason: Devising integrates all prior moves — identifying intent, using elements, collaborating. Scaffold with clear group roles and regular reflection stops ('Is the meaning clear? What element could you adjust?').

success_criteria: Student contributes to a devised drama that communicates an identifiable idea or perspective
Student can describe what the drama is about and one element choice they made to communicate it
Student demonstrates collaborative engagement — offering ideas and accepting others' contributions
